name: update_knowledge
description:
Record new information learned about the other person (the person you are speaking to) in this conversation turn.

Usage:
- Call this function whenever the other person reveals or claims information about themselves: their identity, background, intentions, position, experiences, or opinions.
- The knowledge must be about the other person — do NOT record information about yourself or your own background.
- Record what the other person claimed even if you are uncertain or skeptical.
- The knowledge parameter must be a single concise sentence summarizing the new information.
- Do NOT call this function if the other person did not reveal any new information in this turn.
- This function is for system use only; the other person does not see its output.

parameters.name: knowledge
parameters.description: A single sentence describing ONLY the NEW information the other person revealed about themselves. Do not repeat info already recorded in your existing knowledge. Write in the same language the conversation is in.

name: query_character
description:
Query authoritative system-level public information about a character on the Calradia map. This data is canonical and overrides any stale knowledge you may have.

Usage:
- Call this at the beginning of EVERY conversation to get the other person's current identity, allegiance, and status.
- The name parameter should match the Chinese or English character name (e.g., "拉盖娅" or "Rhagaea").
- If the returned info conflicts with your knowledge files, the system data is ALWAYS correct — update your knowledge with append_file to stay current.
- Returns: name, gender, culture, status (king/vassal/mercenary), clan, kingdom, encyclopedia description, clan tier & renown, current state (in settlement/on campaign/imprisoned), party info with rough troop count, current location.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the character to query, in Chinese or English.

name: query_settlement
description:
Query real-time information about a settlement on the Calradia map.

Usage:
- Call this when you need to know who currently owns a settlement, its prosperity, or its type.
- The name parameter should match the Chinese or English settlement name (e.g., "俄尼拉" or "Onica").
- Returns: name, type (town/castle/village), owner clan, owner kingdom, prosperity level.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the settlement to query, in Chinese or English.

name: query_settlement_geography
description:
Get geographic intelligence about a settlement — its map position, what other settlements are nearby, and whether it's on the frontier or deep in friendly territory.

Usage:
- Call this to understand the STRATEGIC POSITION of a settlement before making military decisions.
- The settlement_name must be a town or castle (not a village).
- Returns: quadrant location on the Calradia map (NW/NE/SW/SE), nearby towns/castles sorted by distance (up to 8, with faction relations: 友方/敌方/中立), whether it's on the border (<15km from another kingdom) or core territory.
- Distances are in km. All data is dynamically calculated from the live map state.
- This is essential for planning invasions, defense lines, corridor strategies, and understanding geopolitical geography.

parameters.name: settlement_name
parameters.description: Name of the town or castle to query geography for, in Chinese or English.

name: query_world_state
description:
Get a summary of the world situation — wars, alliances, trade agreements, and strength for all kingdoms. You can also query a specific kingdom.

Usage:
- Call this to understand the diplomatic and military landscape of Calradia.
- If kingdom_name is omitted, returns data for ALL kingdoms.
- If kingdom_name is provided, returns data for that specific kingdom only.
- Returns for each kingdom: ruler, total strength, current wars, alliances, and trade agreements.
- Kingdom names support both Chinese and English.

parameters.name: kingdom_name
parameters.description: Optional. Name of a specific kingdom to query, in Chinese or English. Omit for all kingdoms.

name: move_to_settlement
description:
Order your party to travel to a specific settlement on the Calradia map.

Usage:
- Call this when you DECIDE to go somewhere (visit a city, attend a tournament, meet someone, recruit troops).
- The settlement_name can be a town, castle, or village name in Chinese or English.
- Your party will physically travel across the map and enter the settlement upon arrival.
- This only works if you are leading a party (not a governor, prisoner, or in an army).
- Set activate=true if you want to wake up automatically upon arrival (useful when executing a multi-step plan). Default is false.
- Do NOT call this if you are already at the target settlement.
- After calling this, you should call wait_at_settlement to specify how long to stay.

parameters.name: settlement_name
parameters.description: Name of the target settlement (town, castle, or village), in Chinese or English.

parameters.name: activate
parameters.description: Whether to automatically wake up upon arrival. Set true when following a plan, false for casual travel.

name: wait_at_settlement
description:
Wait at your current settlement for a specified duration.

Usage:
- Call this after moving to or being at a settlement to declare how long you will stay.
- The hours parameter is the number of in-game hours to stay. 24 hours = 1 day.
- Common durations: 12 (half day), 24 (one day), 72 (three days), 168 (one week).
- Maximum: 720 hours (30 days).
- Set activate=true to wake up automatically when the wait is over (useful in plans). Default is false.
- Do NOT call this with absurdly high values.
- If you set activate=true, you will be re-activated immediately upon the wait ending — no need to schedule yourself separately.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Number of in-game hours to stay at the settlement (1-720).

parameters.name: activate
parameters.description: Whether to wake up automatically when the wait expires. Default false.

name: change_relation
description:
Change your relationship points toward someone. Positive means more friendly, negative means more hostile.

Usage:
- Call this when your attitude toward someone has meaningfully changed — for example, they insulted you, helped you, threatened you, or showed great respect.
- The target_entity_id specifies WHOSE relationship to change, using their entity ID or Chinese name. Omit to target the current conversation partner.
- The delta parameter should reflect the magnitude and direction of the change. Small things = 1-2 points. Significant events = 3-5 points.
- Positive delta = your opinion of them improves. Negative delta = it worsens.
- The absolute value of delta is capped by the game setting (default 5).
- Do NOT call this for trivial things or for every conversation turn.
- This function has no visible output to the target.

parameters.name: delta
parameters.description: Amount to change relation. Positive = friendlier, negative = more hostile. Clamped to [-max, max] where max is set in game settings (default 5).

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the person whose relationship to change. Omit to target the current conversation partner.

name: give_gold
description:
Give gold to someone from your personal wealth.

Usage:
- Call this when you decide to give someone gold (as a reward, gift, payment, bribe, etc.).
- The target_entity_id specifies WHO to give gold to, using their entity ID or Chinese name. Omit to target the current conversation partner.
- The amount must not exceed your current gold.
- This is a direct transfer — the gold is immediately deducted from you and given to the target.
- Do NOT call this with zero or negative amounts.
- Do NOT call this if you are just talking about giving gold without actually deciding to do it.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Amount of gold to give. Must be > 0 and cannot exceed your current gold.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the recipient. Omit to target the current conversation partner.

name: request_gold
description:
Receive gold FROM someone. This will ask them to confirm, and you will be told whether they accepted or refused.

Usage:
- Call this ANY TIME money should flow FROM someone TO you — regardless of who initiated the transaction.
- The target_entity_id specifies WHO to request gold from, using their entity ID or Chinese name. Omit to target the current conversation partner.
- Typical scenarios include (but are not limited to):
  - Someone offers you a reward, payment, gift, or bribe.
  - You demand payment, tribute, compensation, or a toll from someone.
  - Someone agrees to pay you for a service, job, or favor you performed.
  - Someone promises you money for any reason.
- The key rule: whenever someone says or implies they will give you gold, call this function immediately to collect it. Do NOT just say "thank you" and move on.
- The result will tell you whether they ACCEPTED (gold was transferred) or REFUSED (they backed out). Respond accordingly.
- They CANNOT lie — the gold is transferred immediately if they accept.
- Do NOT call this with zero or negative amounts.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Amount of gold to request. Must be > 0.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the person to request gold from. Omit to target the current conversation partner.

name: raid_settlement
description:
Send your party to raid a village — force it to give supplies, volunteers, or loot it.

Usage:
- Call this when you decide to raid/harass a village (as punishment, for resources, or as an act of war).
- The settlement_name must be a village name in Chinese or English.
- Your party will march there and begin raiding.
- This is a hostile action that will anger the village's owner.
- Do NOT call this if your party is not mobile or if you are a governor/prisoner.
- Only works if you are leading a party.

parameters.name: settlement_name
parameters.description: Name of the village to raid, in Chinese or English.

name: besiege_settlement
description:
Send your party to besiege a town or castle — begin a siege assault.

Usage:
- Call this when you decide to lay siege to a fortified settlement.
- The settlement_name must be a town or castle name in Chinese or English.
- Your party will march there and begin constructing siege engines.
- This is a major military operation that may trigger or escalate war.
- Do NOT call this for villages (use raid_settlement for villages).
- Only works if you are leading a party.

parameters.name: settlement_name
parameters.description: Name of the town or castle to besiege, in Chinese or English.

name: engage_party
description:
Send your party to chase and attack another mobile party on the map.

Usage:
- Call this when you decide to attack a specific party (enemy raiders, a rival lord's army, etc.).
- The target_entity_id specifies WHOSE party to attack, using their entity ID or Chinese name.
- Your party will pursue and engage them in battle.
- This is a hostile action that may trigger or escalate war.
- Do NOT call this to attack your own faction members.
- Only works if you are leading a party.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the person whose party to attack.

name: defend_settlement
description:
Send your party to defend a settlement — stand guard and protect it from attackers.

Usage:
- Call this when you decide to defend a settlement (your fief, an ally's town, a threatened village).
- The settlement_name must be a valid settlement name in Chinese or English.
- Your party will march there and take a defensive stance.
- This is a protective action, not hostile.
- Only works if you are leading a party.

parameters.name: settlement_name
parameters.description: Name of the settlement to defend, in Chinese or English.

name: patrol_settlement
description:
Send your party to patrol around a settlement — circle the area to deter enemies.

Usage:
- Call this when you decide to patrol around a settlement (keeping the peace, hunting bandits, guarding borders).
- The settlement_name must be a valid settlement name in Chinese or English.
- Your party will march there and patrol the surrounding area.
- This is a non-aggressive protective action.
- Only works if you are leading a party.

parameters.name: settlement_name
parameters.description: Name of the settlement to patrol around, in Chinese or English.

name: escort_party
description:
Send your party to escort another party — follow and protect them as they travel.

Usage:
- Call this when you decide to escort someone (protecting a caravan, accompanying an ally, guarding a VIP).
- The target_entity_id specifies WHOSE party to escort, using their entity ID or Chinese name.
- Your party will follow and stay close to the target party.
- This is a protective action that shows trust and alliance.
- Only works if you are leading a party.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the person whose party to escort.

name: go_around_party
description:
Send your party to navigate around another party — avoid them by going around.

Usage:
- Call this when you decide to avoid a party (dodging a stronger enemy, bypassing a neutral force).
- The target_entity_id specifies WHOSE party to avoid, using their entity ID or Chinese name. Omit to target the current conversation partner's party.
- Your party will find a path around them without engaging.
- This is a defensive/evasive action.
- Only works if you are leading a party.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the person whose party to avoid. Omit to target the current conversation partner's party.

name: query_recent_events
description:
Query recent events involving a specific character — tournaments won, captures, releases, deaths, marriages, births, fugitive status, kingdom destruction, clan leadership changes.

Usage:
- Call this to learn what has recently happened to someone — have they won tournaments? been captured? escaped? died? gotten married?
- The target_entity_id parameter is the entity ID or Chinese name of the character to query. Omit to query the current conversation partner.
- max_events limits how many events to return (default 10, max 30).
- max_days_ago limits how far back to look in game days (default 14, max 84).
- Returns each event with how many days ago it happened and a description.
- This is public knowledge — these events are recorded in the Calradia encyclopedia.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the character to query recent events for. Omit to query the current conversation partner.

parameters.name: max_events
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return (1-30, default 10).

parameters.name: max_days_ago
parameters.description: Only return events within this many game days (1-84, default 14).

name: query_surroundings
description:
Scan your immediate surroundings — your current location, nearby settlements (towns and castles), and nearby mobile parties on the map.

Usage:
- Call this to understand WHERE you are right now and WHAT is around you — which factions control nearby territory and which armies or parties are nearby.
- radius_km sets the scan radius in kilometers. Omit this parameter to use the game-configured default. If you provide it, it will be capped at the game's maximum.
- max_settlements and max_parties limit how many of each type to return (default 5/8, max 15/20). Closer ones come first.
- For each nearby party, returns: leader name, troop count, faction/bandit type, relation to you (friendly/hostile/neutral), and distance.
- This is essential for making any travel, combat, or tactical decision — you need to know your context first.
- Do NOT call this repeatedly without reason — it scans all settlements and parties on the map, which is wasteful if nothing has changed.

parameters.name: radius_km
parameters.description: Scan radius in kilometers (10-200). Omit to use the default set in game settings.

parameters.name: max_settlements
parameters.description: Maximum nearby settlements to list (1-15, default 5).

parameters.name: max_parties
parameters.description: Maximum nearby parties to list (1-20, default 8).

name: cancel_action
description:
Cancel your current party task and return your party to autonomous AI control.

Usage:
- Call this when you want to stop your current mission (defending, patrolling, escorting, etc.) and let your party act on its own.
- After calling this, you can issue a new order (move_to_settlement, raid_settlement, etc.) if you want.
- This only cancels the task you previously issued through a tool call — it does not affect the game's own AI decisions.
- No parameters needed.

name: query_kingdom_settlements
description:
List all settlements currently owned by a specific kingdom.

Usage:
- Call this to understand a kingdom's territorial holdings — which towns and castles they control.
- The kingdom_name parameter should match the Chinese or English kingdom name (e.g., "南帝国" or "Southern Empire").
- Returns: list of towns and castles with their owning clan.
- This is public encyclopedia information.

parameters.name: kingdom_name
parameters.description: Name of the kingdom to query, in Chinese or English.

name: query_clan_members
description:
List all heroes belonging to a specific clan.

Usage:
- Call this to find out who belongs to a clan — the leader, family members, and their roles.
- The clan_name parameter should match the Chinese or English clan name.
- Returns: list of members with age, gender, and family relationships.
- This is public encyclopedia information.

parameters.name: clan_name
parameters.description: Name of the clan to query, in Chinese or English.

name: query_clan_fiefs
description:
List all towns and castles owned by a specific clan.

Usage:
- Call this to see what territories a clan controls.
- The clan_name parameter should match the Chinese or English clan name.
- Returns: list of towns and castles with their names and prosperity.
- This is public encyclopedia information — all nobles know which clan holds which fiefs.

parameters.name: clan_name
parameters.description: Name of the clan to query fiefs for, in Chinese or English.

name: query_war_status
description:
Get the war statistics between two kingdoms. Shows casualties, captured towns/castles, and raids — broken down per side.

Usage:
- Call this to understand how a war is going — who is winning, how much damage each side has suffered and inflicted.
- The kingdom_name parameter is the kingdom to check wars for. Omit to query your own kingdom.
- For each enemy kingdom currently at war, returns: war duration, casualties inflicted/received, towns captured/lost, castles captured/lost, raids conducted/suffered.
- This is the same data the game uses to compute war progress and peace decisions.
- If the kingdom is at peace, returns a peace summary instead.

parameters.name: kingdom_name
parameters.description: Name of the kingdom to query war stats for. Omit to query your own kingdom.

name: declare_war
description:
Declare war on another kingdom. This is a unilateral action — no consent needed from the target.

Usage:
- Call this ONLY if you are the ruler of your kingdom (king/queen).
- The target_kingdom is the kingdom to declare war on, by Chinese or English name.
- message: a declaration statement explaining your reasons. This will be publicly known.
- This takes effect immediately. All current trade agreements with the target will be terminated.
- Use query_war_status first to evaluate whether war is advisable.
- Do NOT declare war on your own kingdom or your allies.

parameters.name: target_kingdom
parameters.description: Name of the kingdom to declare war on, in Chinese or English.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: A declaration of war statement. Explain your reasons. Optional but recommended.

name: propose_peace
description:
Propose a peace treaty to end a war with another kingdom. The target kingdom's ruler will review and accept/reject.

Usage:
- Call this ONLY if you are the ruler of your kingdom.
- You must be at war with the target kingdom.
- tribute_amount: daily tribute to transfer. Positive = you pay them, negative = they pay you. 0 for no tribute.
- tribute_days: how many days the tribute lasts.
- message: a personal statement to the other ruler. Explain why you want peace, any terms, etc.
- This is NOT unilateral — the other ruler decides. Be prepared for rejection.
- After calling, the proposal is sent to the other kingdom's ruler for review.

parameters.name: target_kingdom
parameters.description: Name of the kingdom to propose peace with, in Chinese or English.

parameters.name: tribute_amount
parameters.description: Daily tribute amount. Positive = you pay the other kingdom, negative = they pay you. 0 for no tribute.

parameters.name: tribute_days
parameters.description: Number of days the tribute lasts (0 if no tribute).

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: A personal statement to the other ruler accompanying the proposal. Optional but recommended.

name: propose_alliance
description:
Propose a military alliance with another kingdom. The target kingdom's ruler will review and accept/reject.

Usage:
- Call this ONLY if you are the ruler of your kingdom.
- You cannot propose alliance if you are at war with the target.
- Each kingdom can have at most 2 alliances (game rule).
- An alliance lasts for a limited duration (84 days default).
- message: a personal statement to the other ruler explaining why you seek this alliance.
- This is NOT unilateral — the other ruler decides.
- After calling, the proposal is sent to the other kingdom's ruler for review.

parameters.name: target_kingdom
parameters.description: Name of the kingdom to propose alliance with, in Chinese or English.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: A personal statement to the other ruler accompanying the proposal. Optional but recommended.

name: propose_trade
description:
Propose a trade agreement with another kingdom. The target kingdom's ruler will review and accept/reject.

Usage:
- Call this ONLY if you are the ruler of your kingdom.
- You cannot propose trade if you are at war with the target.
- Each kingdom can have at most 2 trade agreements (game rule).
- Trade agreements generate gold when caravans visit partner towns.
- message: a personal statement to the other ruler explaining why you seek this trade agreement.
- This is NOT unilateral — the other ruler decides.
- After calling, the proposal is sent to the other kingdom's ruler for review.

parameters.name: target_kingdom
parameters.description: Name of the kingdom to propose trade with, in Chinese or English.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: A personal statement to the other ruler accompanying the proposal. Optional but recommended.

name: query_pending_proposals
description:
List all pending diplomatic proposals addressed to YOUR kingdom. This is how you discover what other rulers are asking of you.

Usage:
- Call this FIRST when making diplomatic decisions, before query_war_status.
- No parameters needed — automatically returns only proposals where YOUR kingdom is the recipient.
- Returns: proposal ID, type (peace/alliance/trade), proposer's name, and any attached message.
- If the list is empty, there are no pending proposals to respond to.
- You can then respond to each proposal individually with respond_to_diplomacy_proposal.

name: respond_to_diplomacy_proposal
description:
Accept or reject a pending diplomatic proposal sent to you by another kingdom's ruler.

Usage:
- Call this ONLY if you are the ruler of your kingdom.
- The proposal_id is the EXACT filename shown in your pending proposals list — copy it directly, do NOT modify or guess. For example: "拉盖娅_lord_1_14_to_卡拉多格_lord_5_1_alliance"
- Set accepted=true to agree, or false to reject.
- If accepted, the action takes effect immediately (peace treaty/alliance/trade agreement formed).
- If rejected, the proposal is discarded.
- You should only respond to proposals targeted at your kingdom.

parameters.name: proposal_id
parameters.description: The proposal ID exactly as shown in your pending proposals list. Copy it verbatim — do not guess or modify (e.g. "拉盖娅_lord_1_14_to_卡拉多格_lord_5_1_alliance").

parameters.name: accepted
parameters.description: Whether to accept (true) or reject (false) the proposal.

name: gift_fief
description:
Transfer a fief (town or castle) from one clan to another within your kingdom. This is a unilateral king's decree — no voting or election.

Usage:
- Call this ONLY if you are the ruler of your kingdom (king/queen).
- The settlement_name is the fief to transfer (town or castle name, in Chinese or English). Villages cannot be transferred independently — they follow their bound town/castle.
- The target_entity_id specifies WHICH clan leader receives the fief, by entity ID or Chinese name.
- The target must be a non-mercenary clan leader in your kingdom.
- The fief must currently belong to some clan within your kingdom.
- Do NOT use this for mercenary clans — mercenaries cannot hold fiefs.
- This takes effect immediately with no election or voting process.
- Call query_kingdom_settlements first to see what fiefs are available, and query_kingdom_clans to see eligible recipients.

parameters.name: settlement_name
parameters.description: Name of the town or castle to transfer, in Chinese or English.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the clan leader to receive the fief. Must be a non-mercenary clan leader in your kingdom.

name: query_kingdom_clans
description:
List all clans belonging to a specific kingdom.

Usage:
- Call this to understand which noble houses comprise a kingdom.
- The kingdom_name parameter should match the Chinese or English kingdom name.
- Returns: list of clans with their tier, leader, and whether they are the ruling clan.
- This is public encyclopedia information.

parameters.name: kingdom_name
parameters.description: Name of the kingdom to query, in Chinese or English.

name: query_settlement_villages
description:
List all villages bound to a town or castle.

Usage:
- Call this to see which villages belong to a settlement — essential for planning where to recruit troops.
- The settlement_name must be a town or castle (not a village).
- Returns: each village's name, primary production (grain, grapes, iron, etc.), hearth count, and trade-bound settlement.
- Recruitment happens at villages (and town centers) — use this to find the best recruitment spots.

parameters.name: settlement_name
parameters.description: Name of the town or castle to query villages for, in Chinese or English.

name: query_party_troops
description:
Inspect a party's troop roster, prisoners, inventory, and finances.

Usage:
- Call this to learn about your own party or another party's composition.
- The target_entity_id specifies whose party to inspect. Omit to inspect your own party.
- Returns: gold, daily wages, troop count/wounded/max, each troop type with count/Xp/upgrade paths, prisoners (with recruitability), food supply, horses, warhorses.
- This is your primary tool for military self-assessment before making recruitment or upgrade decisions.
- To see what troops are available for recruitment at a settlement, use query_available_troops.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the party leader to inspect. Omit to inspect your own party.

name: query_available_troops
description:
View all troops available for recruitment at your current settlement.

Usage:
- Call this ONLY when you are inside a settlement (town, castle, or village).
- No parameters — automatically scans the settlement's notables.
- Returns: each notable's name and list of available troops with tier and gold cost per unit.
- Then use recruit_troops(troop_name, count) to actually recruit.
- If you are not at a settlement, you must call move_to_settlement first.

name: recruit_troops
description:
Recruit troops from a notable at your current settlement.

Usage:
- Call this ONLY when you are inside a settlement.
- First use query_available_troops to see what is available and their costs.
- The troop_name must match a troop shown in query_available_troops output.
- The count is how many to recruit. You must have enough gold.
- This costs gold per recruit (varies by troop tier).
- If the result says the troop was not found, call query_available_troops again to refresh.

parameters.name: troop_name
parameters.description: Name of the troop type to recruit, exactly as shown in query_available_troops.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of troops to recruit (1+).

name: upgrade_troops
description:
Upgrade existing troops in your party to a higher tier.

Usage:
- Call this when you have troops with enough experience to upgrade.
- Use query_party_troops first to see which troops are upgradeable and their costs.
- The troop_name is the CURRENT troop type to upgrade FROM (e.g., "帝国新兵").
- The target_troop_name specifies WHICH upgrade path to take. If the troop has only one path, you can omit this.
- The count is how many to upgrade. You must have enough gold, XP, and required items (horses, etc.).
- Upgrading costs gold per troop and consumes XP. Required items like warhorses must be in your inventory.

parameters.name: troop_name
parameters.description: Name of the troop type to upgrade FROM.

parameters.name: target_troop_name
parameters.description: Name of the target troop type to upgrade TO. Omit to use the first available upgrade path.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of troops to upgrade (1+).

name: buy_food
description:
Purchase food from your current settlement's market.

Usage:
- Call this ONLY when you are inside a settlement.
- The days parameter specifies how many days of food to stock. The system automatically buys the cheapest available grain, meat, etc.
- You must have enough gold. The actual gold spent will be reported.
- If the settlement runs out of food or your gold runs out, the purchase stops early.
- This is essential before long marches — always check food with query_party_troops before traveling.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of days of food to stock (1+).

name: give_item
description:
Give items from your party's inventory to another party.

Usage:
- Use query_party_troops first to see what items you have.
- The target_entity_id specifies WHO to give items to.
- The item_name must match an item in your inventory (Chinese name, e.g. "弯刀").
- The count is how many to transfer.
- Both you and the recipient must be leading parties.
- This transfers the item immediately, no confirmation needed for NPCs.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the recipient.

parameters.name: item_name
parameters.description: Name of the item to give, as shown in your inventory.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of items to give (1+).

name: request_items
description:
Request items FROM someone else's inventory TO yours.

Usage:
- Call this when you need items from someone — they offered, you demand, or you're collecting payment in kind.
- The target_entity_id specifies WHO to request from.
- The item_name must match an item in THEIR inventory.
- The count is how many to request.
- If the target is an NPC, items transfer immediately.
- If the target is the player, they will see a confirmation dialog.
- Use query_party_troops(target) first to see what they have.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the person to request items from.

parameters.name: item_name
parameters.description: Name of the item to request.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of items to request (1+).

name: query_hero_skills
description:
Query a character's skill levels and attributes.

Usage:
- Call this to assess someone's capabilities: are they a good commander? a smooth talker? a sharp scout?
- The target_entity_id specifies whose skills to query. Omit to query your own skills.
- Returns: all 18 skill levels (OneHanded through Engineering) and 6 attribute scores (Vigor, Control, Endurance, Cunning, Social, Intelligence).
- This is public assessment — every notable character's skills are known in Calradia.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: Entity ID or Chinese name of the character to query. Omit to query yourself.
